chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Waltzes and tangos at the Trianon Ballroom
summary: Western dancers wanted waltzes, so the band played pop waltzes and authentic tangos with arrangements from Sampson and Dr. Steel.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Trianon Ballroom -- that's the name of the ballroom. That's where all the big bands played when they came out there. That was the famous Trianon Ballroom.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I mean, they had more people than you ever seen in your life in a ballroom. It was such a huge ballroom.
And when we got to the Trianon -- I want to go back, because this is very funny. We got to the Trianon Ballroom -- that's where we out-did ourselves.
People out in the west like to waltz a lot. And I would take like two hours -- now, Chick Webb had a lot of music, he had a lot of melodies.
He used to get Sampson to make these beautiful waltzes -- (inaudible) for waltzes. All pop tunes, you know, and show tunes a melody, you know.
We had like three or four different sets of these melodies. And then we have a set of just one melody.
We had like two or three sets of all the pop tunes and waltzes -- "Waltzing Down The Lane" -- beautiful things, you know.
So, twice a night -- we had a great big

gong. Boom. This is the waltz time here. (Inaudible) all over.
People would just jump up, hit the floor, you know. And we're going through these beautiful waltzes, you know.
Now, this is one thing that we would do that nobody knew, you know.
The manager of the place didn't know what was going on. Then after that, we would go into some tango.

We had some beautiful tangos that Dr. Steel -- you remember Dr. Steel, the piano player? Doctor of music, he'd (Inaudible) show us how to play these things. Told us (the inaudible) right beat, you know.
"Oh, this is so and so. Right in here so and so." Just like "Viennese Waltz," he say, "Oh, the tempo's too fast," you know.
He showed us how to play, you know.
